classification: Analysis of the actual 300-condition v6 purchase-controller experiment; no production changes
findings: All 180 paired candidate cases fail the strict desired role split: higher Wave for candidate AND higher ordinary crystal/min for Farming.
C uses paid production repairs but its successful deeper runs generally also kill more high-wave enemies, increasing reward points/min.

Current original Record reserves early branch costs at low supply; candidates B and C delay branches and materially improve several weapons. This supports the investment-timing hypothesis, not an all-weapons optimum.

Best candidate median combination is C/Enso: Wave50,590.93sec,7.98crystals/min, versus original best Farming/Resonance: Wave46,543.60sec,7.41crystals/min. It improves both objectives rather than separating them.
For default Point, B gives Wave39.5 vs Farming39; 6/10 paired Wave wins, but farming rate only wins3/10. Not a robust role split.
All candidate clocks align with production purchase boundaries before ticks30,60,...; costs and combat constants are shared.
recommendation: Do not mark G-V2-04/05 role separation passed. Candidate B is a defensible general investment improvement for Point/Bleed/Sweep/Enso, with weapon-dependent failures.

Keep economic and record labels as candidate objectives, or use structural names such as supply-led and repair-reserve. Existing once-only record milestones can supply a separate challenge value without claiming ordinary income/min separation.
limitations: Correlation is descriptive across repeated paired seeds, not causal evidence or statistical significance.
Three candidates exhausted; no fourth candidate or seed filtering.
Tier, forced cashout, hidden build multipliers, enemy weakening and new repair powers were not introduced.
